findings.title: Concurrent builds of the same namespace can replace a newer index with a stale one
findings.body: Removing the mutex around the full build leaves only the final map assignment synchronized. Two concurrent Search requests (or a Search and the watch handler) can both observe a cache miss for the same NamespacedResource and build from different storage snapshots. If the build using the older snapshot completes last, this assignment replaces the index that already included a newer write, and subsequent searches permanently omit that write until another event happens to repair the index. File-backed indexes can also have concurrent bleve.New calls for the same directory. Coordinate builds per cache key (for example with a keyed singleflight/building map) and only publish one reconciled index.

findings.title: Failed eager initialization leaks initialized lifecycle resources and watchers
findings.body: NewResourceServer now returns immediately on s.Init failure without cancelling s.ctx or invoking the Lifecycle Stop hook. This is observable when Lifecycle.Init succeeds but search initialization or initWatcher later fails: the constructor returns no server handle to the caller, while initialized resources remain active. In particular, search.init may already have created its background WatchWriteEvents goroutine before initWatcher fails. Clean up the partially initialized server (cancel it and stop initialized lifecycle components) before returning the construction error.

findings.title: The storage-server integration test is no longer run for PostgreSQL
findings.body: PostgreSQL is a supported unified-storage backend, but this change unconditionally skips this integration test for it. The test therefore no longer validates the storage-server startup path on PostgreSQL, precisely where initialization has moved from the first RPC into construction. The underlying PostgreSQL/Drone failure should be fixed or isolated rather than removing this coverage.
